items.text: Structure on $\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)$

Algebra $A$ (associative, commutative, unitary) $\Longleftrightarrow$ on $V(A)$: a diagonal $\delta\colon V(A)\to V(A)\boxtimes V(A)$ that is coassociative, cocommutative ($s\circ\delta=\delta$), with counit $\varepsilon\colon V(A)\to\mathcal O$ (image of $1\in A$). These data recover $X$.
$X$ inside $\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)$
x\in\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)(k')\ \text{lies in}\ X(k')\iff \delta(x)=x\boxtimes x\ \ \text{and}\ \ \varepsilon(x)=1

Proof: $x\colon A\to k'$ is a ring homomorphism iff $x(1)=1$ (and $\varepsilon(x)=x(1)$) and $x(ab)=x(a)x(b)$, i.e. $x\circ\mu=\mu_{k'}\circ(x\otimes x)$, which is $\delta(x)=x\boxtimes x$ since $\delta$ is the transpose of $\mu$.
Composition law on $X$ and convolution
X\times X\to X\ \leadsto\ \hat\pi\colon\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)\boxtimes\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)=\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X\times X)\to\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)
A law on $X$ = a law $\hat\pi$ on $\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(X)$ compatible with $\delta$ (so that it preserves the subfunctor $X$); it induces $\pi$ on $X$.
$\pi$ associative (commutative) $\iff$ $\hat\pi$ is. $\pi$ has a two-sided unit $\iff$ $\hat\pi$ has a two-sided unit $e$ with $\varepsilon(e)=1$ and $\delta(e)=e\boxtimes e$.
$G$ a monoid: $\operatorname{Dist}(G)$ is an associative algebra (convolution). A bialgebra $A$ = both structures on $V(A)$.
G\hookrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(G)\ \ (\text{units of the algebra of distributions}:\ G\subset\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(G)^{*})
Representations as modules over distributions
$G$ acts on $M$ on the left $\iff$ $\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(G)=V(A)$ acts on $W(M)$ (and on the right on $V(M)$).

$A$ a direct sum of projectives of finite type: $H=\operatorname{Dist}(G)=A^\vee$, a topological algebra (simple convergence), the product continuous; $G$ acts on $M$ $\iff$ $M$ is a left $\operatorname{Dist}(G)$-module with continuous action (factors through a discrete quotient).
Distributions concentrated at the origin
$\varepsilon\colon A\to k$ augmentation, $I=\operatorname{Ker}\varepsilon$, $I$-adic topology on $A$.
\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}_e(G)(k')=\{u\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,k') : u\ \text{vanishes on some power }I^n\}
A subalgebra: the hyperalgebra of $G$ (cf. distributions at the origin of a Lie group, with the convolution product).

\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(G)=\mathcal O\oplus\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}^+(G),\qquad \underline{\operatorname{Dist}}^+=\operatorname{Ker}\bigl(\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(G)\to\underline{\operatorname{Dist}}(e)=\mathcal O\bigr)
The ideal $\operatorname{Dist}^+$ contains the Lie algebra of $G$; its bracket is the bracket of the algebra.
Characteristic $p$: the $p$-th power of a derivation is a derivation; $p$-th power map on the Lie algebra, induced by the $p$-th power in the hyperalgebra.
The same at any section of $G$, by translation.
Example: a constant finite group $\Gamma$
\Gamma_k=\operatorname{Spec}k^{\Gamma},\qquad \operatorname{Dist}(\Gamma_k)=(k^{\Gamma})^{\vee}=k[\Gamma]\ \ (\text{group algebra, multiplication from }\Gamma)
Representations of $\Gamma_k$ on $M$ = representations of the ordinary group $\Gamma$ on $M$ = $k[\Gamma]$-modules.
Lie algebra of $\Gamma_k$ is $0$: $I^2=I$ for the augmentation ideal.
\mathbb Z/2\to\mu_2,\quad 1\mapsto-1:\ \text{isomorphism if }2\text{ is invertible in }k;\ \text{in characteristic }2\ \ \mu_2\ \text{is infinitesimal with a non-zero Lie algebra}

In characteristic $2$: for the generator $x$ of $\operatorname{Lie}\mu_2$, $x^2=x$ in the hyperalgebra, non-trivial. $\mu_p$, $\alpha_p$ have non-trivial Lie algebras; groups from ordinary groups are étale.
